title: King Sorrow
author: Joe Hill
review:
3.5/5 really enjoyed some of the moments of the book but as a cohesive work it has some major issues. Weirdly needs to be longer or change what it focuses on as some of the aspects of the book don't feel connected and doesn't have a solid through line from beginning to end.

The focus of current events and politics was kind of a big miss for me, was more interested in the ties to mythology and Arthurian tales, but it's definitely a weird balance between the two that's not always effective.

Joe Hill is really good at mixing the grittyness of real life with some of the fantasy/mythology elements though so I thought these parts were well done. The depth of the characters was weirdly inconsistent though, sometimes they felt deep and rich and other times they felt like shallow caricatures.
